provenance: Tower of Hanoi requires 2^N - 1 moves; enumerating them costs ~tokensPerMove tokens each, so output length explodes past a fixed token budget. Shojaee et al. 2025 ('The Illusion of Thinking') report accuracy 'collapse' past a complexity threshold; Lawsen 2025 rebut that the collapse is largely a token-limit / evaluation artifact and that some River-Crossing instances are mathematically impossible for N>=6. y here = enumeration-scored accuracy (collapses when tokens exceed budget). Both sources are preprints; this page lets the reader adjudicate.
